# Josupeit.Practices.Schedulers.Channel

> `ChannelScheduler`, an `IScheduler` with an `AsyncService` lifecycle: items go into an unbounded `System.Threading.Channels` queue and are dequeued in FIFO order by a fixed number of consumers (`DegreeOfParallelism`, default `Environment.ProcessorCount`); with one consumer, items run strictly one after another. `PauseAsync` stops dequeuing without dropping anything; `StopAsync` declines everything still queued and gives running items `GracefulStopDelay` (default 3 seconds) before signaling their token. Must be started before use: `Schedule*` on an unstarted or stopped instance throws `InvalidOperationException`. Two types, `ChannelScheduler` and `ChannelSchedulerOptions`; built on `Josupeit.Practices.Schedulers.Core`. Targets netstandard2.0, netstandard2.1, netcoreapp3.0, and net8.0; lives in the `Josupeit.Practices.Schedulers` namespace.

Install with `dotnet add package Josupeit.Practices.Schedulers.Channel`. The types live in the `Josupeit.Practices.Schedulers` namespace - not `Josupeit.Practices.Schedulers.Channel`. Two types:

- `ChannelSchedulerOptions` - `int DegreeOfParallelism` (default `Environment.ProcessorCount`, validated `> 0` at `StartAsync`) and `TimeSpan GracefulStopDelay` (default 3 s; `> 0` cancel running items after, `== 0` at once, `< 0` never); parameterless constructor, mutable, read when used
- `ChannelScheduler : AsyncSchedulerService` - constructor `(ChannelSchedulerOptions options)`, `CanPause` is `true`; inherits `StartAsync`/`StopAsync`/`PauseAsync`/`ResumeAsync`/`State` and all 56 `IScheduler` members; `protected virtual Task ConsumeAsync(CancellationToken)` runs once per consumer

Submission never waits (unbounded channel, no back-pressure). Items are dequeued in FIFO order by the consumer loops (dedicated threads that continue on the thread pool after their first asynchronous wait; never the submitting thread); at most `DegreeOfParallelism` run at once, and only with a degree of one is the start order strict. Pause acts between items and never interrupts a running one. Stop declines queued items with `ExecutionDeclinedException`, signals running items' tokens after `GracefulStopDelay`, and returns only when every running item has actually returned. Scheduling while `Stopped` or `Stopping` is `InvalidOperationException`, not `ExecutionDeclinedException`. Not disposable; restartable.
